fieldValues.title: The .srs repository marker is a directory; its non-emptiness convention is spec, the satisfying file is implementation-owned
fieldValues.decision_rationale:
srs#313 (closed 2026-08-02) found the spec and the implementation disagreeing about the `.srs` marker's kind: the spec's prose called it a file ("empty, or containing a format version on its first line"), while RFC-038, `srs-usage.md`, and every srs-rust code path (`detect.rs find_repo_root`, `FileStore::repository_exists` via `is_dir`, the `.srs/.gitkeep` emission in `tree_session.rs`/`archive.rs`/`srsj.rs`) already agreed it was a directory. The owner's ruling on that issue, made in comments on 2026-08-02, had four numbered parts: (1) the marker is a directory — Invariant 45 and the spec prose (`srs-spec.md:2491`) were the sites that needed to change; RFC-038 [R5] and `repository_exists()`'s `is_dir` already agreed and stood. (2) Non-emptiness is a *convention*, not a normative rule justified by git: the empty-directory loss is a VCS limitation — an implementation concern, not a property of the SRS format — so the spec does not encode around it; the convention stands on its own terms. (3) The default member is an "About SRS" README, whose purpose is discovery and LLM orientation for a reader landing cold in the repository — not merely keeping the directory alive under git; surviving git is a side effect of the file being worth having, not its justification. (4) Drafting that README is deferred to its own task (srs#340, transferred to srs-rust#1066).

Commit 88323e2 folded part (1) into Invariant 45 and the `ext:repository` mechanism the same day. Parts (2)-(4) were never folded into a `rfc-decision-*` record — the ruling existed only in the srs#313 issue thread, with no home in the decision log `srs/srs-usage.md` and the compass point to. This record closes that gap retroactively: it is recording a ruling made on 2026-08-02, not making a new one.

A first draft of this record got part (2) wrong: it justified the README by the git round-trip argument the owner had already rejected in the same thread (the reasoning that sank `.gitkeep` as a candidate: "a git artifact leaking into a format specification"). The owner corrected this on 2026-09-16. The convention stands on discovery/orientation value (part 3), not VCS accommodation; and *which* file discharges it is an implementation choice srs-rust can change independently, tracked at srs-rust#1066. Naming `.srs/README.md` specifically in a spec decision record would also over-specify: under the convention as actually ruled, no new file is required everywhere — the spec repo's own `.srs/profiles/foundation.json` already satisfies non-emptiness, and binding the spec to a filename would make that already-conforming repository non-conformant until it grew a file it does not need.
fieldValues.decision_statement:
(1) The `.srs` repository marker is a directory, not a file. A conforming repository's marker is `is_dir(".srs")`, matching Invariant 45, the `ext:repository` mechanism, and RFC-038 [R5]. This ratifies, retroactively, the ruling the owner made on srs#313 (2026-08-02) and that commit 88323e2 already folded into normative text.

(2) The marker directory's non-emptiness is a convention (SHOULD), not a MUST justified by git. An emptied `.srs/` does not fail silently: `repository_exists()`'s `is_dir` check returns false and the tool reports "not an SRS repository" at first use — a loud but misdiagnosable failure (a documentation problem, not a conformance problem), which is why this is a convention rather than a hard rule. The spec does not encode a VCS's limitation (git drops empty directories) as a property of the SRS format; the convention stands on its own terms, independent of git.

(3) The convention's default member is an "About SRS" orientation document, whose purpose is discovery and LLM orientation for a reader who lands cold in the repository — not merely keeping the directory alive under git (that survival is a side effect of the file being worth having, not its justification).

(4) *Which* file discharges the convention — its name, its contents, and the command that generates it — is delegated to the implementation and is not decided by this record. Drafting the orientation document is its own deferred task, currently srs-rust#1066 (transferred from srs#340), proposing `.srs/README.md` to replace the `.gitkeep` placeholder `repo create` emits today — `.gitkeep` was itself considered and rejected on srs#313 as "a git artifact leaking into a format specification." `.srs/` contents remain implementation-private and outside conformance per RFC-038 [R5] — the repository walk skips `.srs/`, so nothing inside it, whatever file is chosen, can trip [R24] fatality or carry a conformance rule, a schema element, or a semantic claim (CC-43 names this drift-to-normative hazard; this boundary is the standing mitigation). This record does not name a file: under the convention as ruled, `srs/.srs/profiles/foundation.json` already satisfies non-emptiness for the spec repo itself, which needs no README to comply.
fieldValues.decision_scope: Governs the `.srs` marker's kind (directory, part 1), the convention-not-MUST status of its non-emptiness and the reasoning for that status (part 2), the discovery/orientation purpose of its conventional default member (part 3), and the delegation of selecting and producing that member to the implementation (part 4) — across every SRS repository (spec, srs-rust, srs-vscode, and any conforming corpus). Does not name a file, does not author one, and does not reopen RFC-038 [R5] or Invariant 45. Does not decide srs-rust#1066's own design — that stays implementation-owned and owner-merge gated there.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered:
Migrate the implementation to a marker *file* instead — the alternative srs#313 itself named. Rejected: every implementation code path already treated the marker as a directory before the spec was consulted (RFC-038 [R5] predates this ruling); the corpus's disagreement was the spec being wrong, not the implementation.

Make non-emptiness a MUST rather than a SHOULD — considered, since an emptied `.srs/` does make `repository_exists()` return false. Rejected: the failure is loud (the tool reports "not an SRS repository"; it does not silently misbehave) but misdiagnosable — a documentation/tooling problem, not a conformance violation to enforce at the format level. Encoding it as a hard rule would also mean encoding around one VCS's limitation (git drops empty directories), which the spec should not assume every SRS repository even uses.

Name `.gitkeep` as the convention's satisfying file — the status quo `repo create` still emits. Rejected on srs#313 itself: "a git artifact leaking into a format specification. SRS repositories need not live in git, and the spec should not assume they do." `.gitkeep` is not treated here as a neutral baseline the README merely improves on; it is a rejected form still shipping, tracked for replacement at srs-rust#1066.

Name `.srs/README.md` specifically in this decision record — an earlier draft of this record did exactly that, and the owner identified it as a second instance of the same over-specification (2026-09-16). Rejected: the spec's job is to state the convention and its purpose (discovery/orientation, part 3), not pick a filename the implementation is free to change; the spec repo's own `.srs/profiles/foundation.json` already satisfies non-emptiness today, so binding the spec to `README.md` would make an already-conforming repository non-conformant until it grew a file it does not need. Recording a filename would also recreate exactly the coupling this ruling avoids: a later srs-rust rename would require amending a spec decision record rather than closing an implementation issue.

Doing nothing (leaving parts (2)-(4) of the srs#313 ruling unrecorded, as they were for six weeks) was also live and is what actually happened until now — rejected because it is the gap this record closes.
fieldValues.accepted_costs: The convention is a SHOULD, not a MUST: `repo validate` cannot detect an emptied `.srs/` as a conformance error, because by the time `repository_exists()`'s `is_dir` check fails the directory no longer reads as a repository at all — the failure surfaces as "not an SRS repository", not as a diagnostic, which can misdirect debugging toward "this isn't a repo" rather than "this repo lost its marker's placeholder". This record accepts that cost rather than promoting the convention to a MUST, per part (2)'s reasoning. It also accepts that, until srs-rust#1066 lands, `repo create` keeps emitting the rejected `.gitkeep` placeholder rather than the oriented README the ruling calls for; this record does not close that gap, it only confirms the convention and hands the choice of file to the implementation.
evidence_refs: srs#313 (closed 2026-08-02) — the four-part ruling this record captures retroactively: directory kind, non-emptiness as convention (not git-justified), README as the default member for discovery/orientation, and drafting deferred; the ruling existed only in issue comments, never as a decision record, until now

commit 88323e2 — "fix(spec): fold .srs marker directory decision into canonical spec (#313)", folding part (1) into Invariant 45 and the ext:repository mechanism, migrating docs/spec/examples/gallery-project-v2/.srs from file to directory
invariant-045 (e1000045-0000-4000-a000-000000000045) — "A conforming repository must have a `.srs` marker directory and a `manifest.json` at its root"

mechanism-d453219f (Repository layout) — states the marker SHOULD contain a regular file so it survives round-trips; its prose currently also names `.srs/README.md` as 'by convention' — this record's part (4) treats that as illustrative only, not a spec commitment to a filename, since choosing the file is implementation-owned
RFC-038 [R5] — codifies the directory reading; the repository walk skips `.srs/`, so [R24] fatality does not reach inside it

CC-43 (srs#313 ruling thread's hazard ledger) — names the risk of `.srs/` contents drifting into normative weight; RFC-038 [R5]'s walk-skip is the standing mitigation this record relies on in part (4)
srs-rust#1066 (open, gate:owner-merge, transferred from srs#340) — tracks drafting the "About SRS" orientation document that will replace `.gitkeep`, constrained to never become authoritative
srs-rust#691 (filed 2026-07-22) — "Spec/impl divergence: .srs marker is a file in the spec, a directory in the implementation"; this ruling's part (1) resolves it
fieldValues.review_trigger: Review if any future normative edit to Invariant 45 or the ext:repository mechanism reintroduces a git/VCS-based justification for non-emptiness — the ruling's part (2) is explicit that the convention stands on its own terms, not as an accommodation to git. Also review if mechanism-d453219f's prose is ever read as committing the spec to `.srs/README.md` specifically rather than illustrating one candidate — if so, tighten it (Door 3) to state the convention without naming a file, matching this record's part (4). Finally, review when srs-rust#1066 lands: this record's part (4) should then be checked against the file it actually produces, to confirm the delegation held and no normative claim crept into `.srs/` content along the way.
